To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a click chemistry approach was used for the synthesis of novel benzenesulfon- and 2.3.5.6-tetra-fluorobenzen- and 2-hydroxybenzenesulfon-amide inhibitors of the cyto-solic carbonic anhy-drase isoforms I and Ii, and of the tumor-associated isoforms ix and xii.

A click chemistry approach has been used to synthesize a new series of benzene- and tetrafluorobenzene-sulfonamides, which have been evaluated as inhibitors of the cytoplasmic carbonic anhydrases (hCA I and II) and the tumor-associated isoforms (hCA IX and XII).
we have synthesized novel sulfonamide inhibitors of CAs by using a click approach, and we have determined the X-ray structure of the hCA II complex with two of these compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of new sulfonamide CAIs incorporating the click chemistry strategy.
the synthesis of new CA inhibitors, which can be used for the design of novel anticancer drugs.
the development of new inhibitors for carbonic anhydrases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of electron withdrawing groups on the aromatic ring and of the alkyl chain of sulfonamides increases the potency of inhibition of the cytosol isoforms of carbonic anhydrases, while it decreases the potency of inhibition against the tumor-associated CA isoforms IX and XII.

the click chemistry approach is very useful to generate a large number of novel sulfonamide inhibitors of CA isoforms, with the possibility to introduce a variety of substituents at the aryl ring and at the alkyl side chain of the sulfonamide moiety, which can modulate the inhibitory power and selectivity of these compounds.

the click chemistry approach is a powerful tool for the synthesis of novel sulfonamides, which are endowed with CA inhibitory properties and can be used as pharmacological tools in the study of the physiological and pathological roles of this enzyme superfamily.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new compounds obtained by the click chemistry approach are good inhibitors of the CAs, with a potential for the development of new drugs for the treatment of different pathologies, including cancer, glaucoma, edemas, and obesity.
the new sulfonamides obtained via click chemistry are potent inhibitors of the CA isoforms I, II, IX, and XII and that they can be used as lead compounds for the development of new CA inhibitors.
the click chemistry strategy can be applied to a large number of CA inhibitors, which can be used as lead compounds in drug design.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a 3,4,5-trifluoromethylphenyl ring on the benzene ring of the sulfonamide moiety of these inhibitors is responsible for the subnanomolar potency observed with the tumor-associated isoforms hCA IX and hCA XII.

the presence of the tetrafluorobenzene moiety in the sulfonamides leads to a higher potency of inhibition, and that the presence of an aminoalkyl chain in the sulfonamide moiety leads to a higher selectivity for the tumor-associated CAs IX and XII isoform, over the cytosolic ones.

the click approach is very efficient to obtain sulfonamide-based CA inhibitors, with the possibility to incorporate different moieties on the sulfonamide group and/or the linker, which can be used to modulate the pharmacokinetic properties of these inhibitors.
